description: Make translations actually appear in the overlay by fixing the four confirmed root causes in the OCR->translation->overlay data flow. This is the primary user complaint: with a GW2 skill tooltip (e.g. 'Plaguelands') clearly on screen, no translation shows. The dictionary DATA is correct (skills.json contains per-line entries like {"en":"Plaguelands",...} and the full description line); the MATCHING and IMAGE PREPROCESSING are broken. This feature is independent of FEAT-002 (drag modifier) except that both touch imgui_overlay.cpp; do FEAT-001 first if serialized.
steps: BUG C (image preprocessing) in src/ocr/ocr_engine.cpp OcrEngine::recognize(): BEFORE SetImage, convert the incoming BGRA buffer (bytesPerPixel==4, layout B,G,R,A per pixel; also handle bytesPerPixel==3 BGR defensively) into a NEW 1-byte-per-pixel grayscale buffer where each output pixel = 255 - ((B+G+R)/3). This does grayscale + INVERT in one pass so GW2's light-text-on-dark-tooltip becomes dark-text-on-light (Tesseract 4.x/5.x expects dark text on light background per https://tesseract-ocr.github.io/tessdoc/ImproveQuality.html) and drops the alpha channel (Tesseract 4.x blends alpha with white, wrecking light-on-dark). Store the grayscale buffer in a std::vector<uint8_t> sized width*height. Then call m_impl->api->SetImage(gray.data(), width, height, 1, width) (bytes_per_pixel=1, bytes_per_line=width). Keep SetRectangle(0,0,width,height). Do NOT pass the original BGRA buffer to SetImage anymore. Keep the vector alive until after GetUTF8Text() is called (SetImage does not copy in all Tesseract versions; the safest contract is to keep the buffer alive through recognition, which it naturally is as a function-local).
BUG D (page segmentation) in OcrEngine::initialize(): change SetPageSegMode(tesseract::PSM_SPARSE_TEXT) to SetPageSegMode(tesseract::PSM_SINGLE_BLOCK) for clean multi-line block reading of a tooltip.

BUG A (line-by-line matching) - restructure recognition so EACH text LINE is looked up independently. Keep OcrEngine::recognize() returning the whole multi-line text + region-level confidence (it still runs GetUTF8Text on the preprocessed grayscale image). Do the line splitting at the translation boundary OR in recognizeRegions - choose the cleanest: recommended approach is to split in Translator::translateBatch (see translator step) so OcrResult stays a single multi-line blob and OcrEngine is unchanged in shape aside from preprocessing/PSM. Whichever layer splits, split on '\n', trim leading/trailing whitespace (space/tab/CR) from each line, and skip empty lines.

BUG D (confidence) in OcrEngine::recognizeRegions(): the current region-level gate 'result.confidence >= m_confidenceThreshold' can wrongly drop a whole mixed-content region. Lower the effective default (handled via config in a later step) AND make the gate not discard everything: keep the region-level MeanTextConf check but at the lowered threshold (40). Keep '!result.text.empty()'. Per-line confidence is not easily available from GetUTF8Text alone, so region-level at threshold 40 is acceptable; document this in a comment.
src/ocr/ocr_engine.h: default m_confidenceThreshold to 40.0f (was 60.0f) to match the new config default and keep header/impl consistent.

BUG B (surface matched AND unmatched lines) in src/translation/translator.h: add a bool field 'matched' to struct TranslationResult (default false). In src/translation/translator.cpp translateBatch(): for EACH OcrResult, split its .text on '\n', trim each line, skip empties, and for each non-empty line call translate(line). If translate() returns a value, push a TranslationResult with matched=true (original=line, translated=dictionary value). If NO match, STILL push a TranslationResult with matched=false, original=line, translated=line (raw OCR text) so the overlay can show what OCR read. This makes 'Plaguelands' on its own line match, the description line match, and any unmatched line still be visible. Preserve the LRU cache use inside translate() for matched lookups.

Translator::translate() (single-string) is unchanged - it still returns nullopt on no match and caches matches; translateBatch owns the raw-fallback behavior. Confirm translate() sets result.matched appropriately if the field is set there; simplest: set matched=true where it constructs a found TranslationResult, and translateBatch sets matched=false for the raw fallback entries. Ensure every code path that constructs a TranslationResult sets .matched explicitly to avoid relying on default only.
BUG marshalling redesign in src/ocr/ocr_api.h: add 'int matched;' field to struct BroncoOcrResult (1=dictionary match, 0=raw OCR line). Keep it a C-ABI-safe plain int.

src/ocr/ocr_api.cpp bronco_ocr_process_frame(): the old code mapped ocrResults[i] 1:1 to translations[i], which breaks now that ONE region yields MULTIPLE lines. Redesign: after translateBatch returns a vector<TranslationResult> (already one entry per recognized line across all regions), iterate that vector and write ONE BroncoOcrResult per entry into outResults, up to the caller-provided capacity. The out-array capacity: currently bronco_ocr_process_frame has no explicit capacity parameter (outResults + outResultCount). Treat the caller contract as: outResults has at least as many slots as the loader allocated (see loader step, 64). Add a hard cap constant (e.g. kMaxResults derived from a #define or a parameter) - since the signature cannot change without touching the loader, use a fixed safe cap of 64 and STOP writing when count reaches 64 to avoid overflow. Map region geometry: since translateBatch flattens across regions, associate geometry from the region the line came from. Simplest robust approach: because follow-mouse mode uses a single region, and even multi-region fixed mode, attach the FIRST region's geometry (regions[0]) to every emitted line, OR better: have translateBatch/marshalling track which region each line came from. Choose the approach that keeps geometry correct: iterate ocrResults; for each ocrResult split into lines; per line do the lookup and emit a BroncoOcrResult carrying THAT ocrResult's region geometry and confidence. Implement the line-splitting in ocr_api.cpp directly if that keeps region association cleanest (call handle->translator on each line via a per-line translate call), rather than relying on translateBatch to flatten. Ensure resultStorage keeps each emitted line's original+translated strings alive (one ResultStorage per emitted line) and that outResults[k].originalText/translatedText point into resultStorage.back() correctly (reserve resultStorage to avoid reallocation invalidating earlier c_str() pointers - reserve BEFORE the loop with an upper bound, or push_back all storage first then assign pointers in a second pass). CRITICAL: std::vector reallocation invalidates c_str() pointers of earlier elements; either reserve resultStorage to the max count up front, or assign the const char* pointers in a SECOND pass after all storage is populated. Use the two-pass or reserve approach explicitly.

src/ocr/ocr_loader.cpp OcrLoader::processFrame(): currently does outResults.resize(regionCount) which gives too few slots for multi-line output. Change to allocate a fixed capacity of 64 slots (outResults.resize(64) or a named constant) before calling m_fnProcessFrame, pass outResults.data(), then outResults.resize(resultCount) on success. Keep clearing on failure. This matches the 64 cap in ocr_api.cpp.

src/pipeline/pipeline.cpp: KEEP the existing OCR-text + dictionary-match logging loop (do not remove bronco::log::info lines). It already builds bronco::overlay::TranslatedEntry from each BroncoOcrResult. Add propagation of the new 'matched' flag: set entry.matched = (result.matched != 0). Keep setting geometry x/y/width/height. Keep calling bronco::overlay::setTranslations(overlayEntries). Update the 'translationFound' log heuristic to use result.matched instead of the (translated != original) heuristic, since raw fallback entries now have translated==original by design.
src/overlay/imgui_overlay.h: add 'bool matched = false;' to struct TranslatedEntry.

src/overlay/imgui_overlay.cpp render(): when iterating g_translations, render MATCHED entries prominently (e.g. normal/bright color, show the translated text, optionally the original dimmer) and UNMATCHED entries in a dimmer secondary style (e.g. ImGui::TextColored with a gray ImVec4 like (0.55f,0.55f,0.55f,1.0f)) showing the raw recognized text so the user can SEE OCR is working. Use entry.matched to branch. Keep ImGui::TextWrapped for wrapping. Do not change unrelated overlay logic.
src/config/config.h: change m_ocrConfidenceThreshold default from 60.0f to 40.0f.

After all edits, re-read EACH modified function end to end: verify no variable is used outside its declaring block (the prior build's failure class), all identifiers declared, Tesseract signatures exact (SetImage(const unsigned char*, int, int, int, int)), GetUTF8Text result freed with delete[], braces balanced, and that resultStorage c_str() pointers are not invalidated by vector growth.
acceptance_criteria: OcrEngine::recognize builds a grayscale+inverted 1-byte-per-pixel buffer and calls SetImage(buf,w,h,1,w); it no longer passes BGRA (4bpp) to SetImage.
Recognized multi-line text is split into individual lines, each trimmed, each looked up independently; a line equal to 'Plaguelands' (case-insensitive) resolves via skills.json.
translateBatch emits an entry for EVERY non-empty recognized line: matched lines carry the translation (matched=true) and unmatched lines carry the raw OCR text (matched=false).

bronco_ocr_process_frame emits one BroncoOcrResult per recognized line, never writes past a 64-slot cap, and its returned const char* pointers remain valid (resultStorage not reallocated after pointer assignment).
OcrLoader::processFrame allocates >= 64 result slots and resizes to resultCount after the call.
TranslatedEntry and BroncoOcrResult carry a matched flag; the overlay renders matched entries prominently and unmatched raw lines dimmer.
ocr_confidence_threshold default is 40 in both config.h and config/bronco_config.json; the region-level confidence gate uses the lowered threshold.
pipeline.cpp still logs OCR text and dictionary-match outcome (now keyed off result.matched).
verification: Cannot build locally (Windows/MSVC/vcpkg). Re-read every edited function to confirm C++ correctness: all identifiers in scope (no block-scoped variable used outside its block), exact types, Tesseract API signatures, matching braces, delete[] on GetUTF8Text, no c_str() dangling from vector reallocation.

Trace the data flow on paper for a follow-mouse region whose OCR yields 'Plaguelands\n<description line>\n<unmatched stat line>' and confirm: 3 lines split, 2 matched + 1 raw fallback, 3 BroncoOcrResult emitted within cap, 3 overlay entries with correct matched flags, overlay renders 2 prominent + 1 dim.
Confirm grep: SetPageSegMode uses PSM_SINGLE_BLOCK; SetImage uses bytes_per_pixel 1; config default 40.0f; bronco_config.json ocr_confidence_threshold 40.
findings: Implemented all steps. (C) ocr_engine.cpp recognize(): added BGRA/BGR -> 1-byte grayscale+invert (out=255-((B+G+R)/3)) into a function-local std::vector<uint8_t> sized w*h, then SetImage(gray.data(),w,h,1,w); no longer passes BGRA to SetImage; buffer stays alive through GetUTF8Text(); added width/height<=0 guard. (D) initialize() now SetPageSegMode(PSM_SINGLE_BLOCK). Region-level confidence gate kept but documented and driven by lowered threshold (default 40). ocr_engine.h m_confidenceThreshold default -> 40.0f. (A/B) translator.h TranslationResult gained bool matched (default false); translate() sets matched=true on dictionary hit; translateBatch() now splits each OcrResult.text on '\n', trims (space/tab/CR), skips empties, emits matched entries and raw-fallback (matched=false, translated==original) entries. Marshalling: ocr_api.h BroncoOcrResult gained int matched and BRONCO_OCR_MAX_RESULTS(64); bronco_ocr_process_frame() redesigned to split each region's text into lines IN the C API (so region geometry/confidence attaches per line), translate each line, emit one BroncoOcrResult per non-empty line, cap at 64, and reserve resultStorage to 64 BEFORE the loop so c_str() pointers never dangle from reallocation. ocr_loader.cpp processFrame allocates BRONCO_OCR_MAX_RESULTS slots then resizes to resultCount. pipeline.cpp sets entry.matched=(result.matched!=0) and keys the OCR log off result.matched instead of the translated!=original heuristic; kept geometry + setTranslations. imgui_overlay.h TranslatedEntry gained bool matched; render() shows matched entries in default bright color and unmatched raw OCR lines dimmer via PushStyleColor(ImGuiCol_Text, ImVec4(0.55,0.55,0.55,1)). config.h default 60->40; bronco_config.json ocr_confidence_threshold 60.0->40. Did NOT touch FEAT-002 drag modifier (isAltHeld/VK_MENU untouched). Cannot build locally (Windows/MSVC/vcpkg); verified by careful re-read: no block-scoped variable used out of scope, exact Tesseract signatures, GetUTF8Text freed with delete[], resultStorage reserved to avoid c_str() invalidation. Grep-confirmed: PSM_SINGLE_BLOCK, SetImage(...,1,width), config defaults 40.
